title: Belgium Tests Europe's Limits: Wildfire Crisis and Stubborn Inflation Strain… · 26 Aug
keywords: Belgium, wildfire, civil protection, climate resilience, consumer confidence, inflation, Eurostat, euro area, EU climate policy, household finances, emergency response, cost of living, Belgium economy, extreme weather, European Union
notes: Belgium's largest recorded wildfire has exposed significant gaps in the country's civil protection and climate-resilience infrastructure, forcing the government to promise a national action plan after emergency services required Dutch helicopters and EU aircraft to contain the blaze. Meanwhile, Belgian households are growing more cautious as inflation remains elevated at 3.6 percent, well above levels that would signal a genuine end to the cost-of-living squeeze. Together, the two crises present a pointed test of whether European governments can maintain citizen trust on both physical security and economic stability. The answer, for now, appears uncertain.
